Question: Would you marry someone like Jenny from the movie "Forrest Gump"?
Answer: Plain and simple. NO. But I would be her friend and attempt to help her back on track. How about 'Would you marry someone like Jenny if you were Forrest Gump?’ As tragic as Jenny's short life and childhood was, marrying her would've been a big mistake. ***Prepare for Spoilers and Cynical Opinions*** Yes Jenny had to deal with serious trauma based on poverty and the abuse she got from her father as a child but that doesn't mean marrying her would've been a neat final chapter in her life and a pleasant experience for Forrest. The real argument is whether she transformed into a decent character towards the end of the movie worth marrying. She kicked her drug habit, promiscuity and adopted a more modest lifestyle. However people who argue that she is the classic case of 'people can change’ fail to look at some of her actions which were just as bad (in some cases worse) while clean. Forgive me but Jenny is not the marrying type for a guy like Forrest or anyone who puts their heart on their sleeve.

Answer: I rented a ratty, hole in the wall apartment for a brief period when I went to University. I say ratty because the very first night I moved in I opened my door later to see a huge rat scampering off behind some junk near the wall. The fat, insolent bugger looked as though he was accustomed to tenants putting out garbage that hour. It was an old building that was sectioned off into a few rooms which in time were further subdivided into smaller rooms. It was like a barracks but ugly, poorly designed and devoid of any taste whatsoever. The entire upstairs and downstairs each shared one tiny kitchen and one bathroom area. I wondered what was the need for a door to the bathroom when there was a gap from the door to the door frame that was so wide you could peep in and see clearly anyone who was having a bath or a shit. As one could imagine it was rented solely by lesser income bracket males. It was a common to see tasteless, junky buildings such as this in any highly populated area in Trinidad. Practically zero laws were enforced in regards to building code so it seemed as though the owners were all competing to build the biggest, ugliest brick and mortar ant-nest in the world. The neighbouring building was no exception but it was a larger, newer and much more spacious apartment complex. The apartment was rented by students who clearly belonged to upper middle class families. The large spacious building was so tall and stately that it seemed to look down on our decrepit little hovel like a deformed, underdeveloped sibling. One night as I lay on my thin mattress, deciding whether to bear with the heat of the poorly ventilated cell-like room or open the window and bear with the plague of mosquitoes waiting patiently to enter I heard a noise that resonated in my ears and in my groin. It was the sound of female laughter. It wasn't just any laughter. It was the lusty, playful laughter of a pair of attractive young women. I looked at the window and saw an open door from the second floor apartment next door and from inside the door the well lit room revealed a girl walking several times past the door completely naked. One could imagine how a lonely, young, hot-blooded male cramped in a tiny room without a single form of entertainment at his disposal would feel to see this tender female figure darting back and forth in front of his eyes without a thread of clothing. It was like seeing flashes of heaven. I quickly turned off my lights so the girl wouldn't catch me peeping and I rooted myself by the window, hungry for more. However nothing else happened and the door closed. The following evening I was home at night trying to read a book on Investments when my ears pricked. The familiar sound of laughter could be heard. Almost on instinct I flew to my light switch and turned it off. I went to the window. This time two girls darted back and forth, nude, in front of the door. I wondered if I was dreaming. At one point, one of them stood by the doorway for several seconds, looking at her phone, allowing one to absorb the view of her body. ‘Somebody’s going to see us,’ one of them said and the mischievous nymphs laughed heartily. They both couldn't be older than 20 and from the way they interacted they were quite possibly related. It was obvious that they both enjoyed exhibition. This was not an accident. I looked at my watch. It was 6:45pm. It was around this time yesterday that one of them gave their show. Immediately the door closed for the night. The show was over. At 6:30 the following evening I was like a perverted sentry posted at my windowsill in the darkness, resolute on catching a third viewing. I wished to God I had had the means to buy binoculars. Why couldn't I been born to a well off family and living in the apartment next to them? I saw them as they came from their classes, heading towards their apartment; a pair of Indian girls, bespectacled and quite innocent looking the way they postured themselves and wore rather baggy, unbecoming clothes. In attire they were completely different creatures, almost nerdy. They looked the dictionary image of graduates from an all girls’ Convent school. They both appeared somber and reticent. They dragged themselves forward without a word to one another and went indoors, closing the door behind them halfway. What was with the moodiness? Did someone report them? Did their family find out about their exhibitions and issued a stern warning? Did someone record them and circulated their nude videos around campus? I hoped to God not. In my steaming little hovel I was hungry for more. I could hear them arguing about something for a few seconds. I could hear them laughing. I could hear them eating. I could hear the dishes being washed and packed away. C’mon! I looked at my watch. It was a minute or so before 7pm. Was tonight going to be a no-show? As the thought came to mind the door opened and the younger girl stepped forward staring at her phone, naked as the Sahara. She stood for a few seconds, myself completely succumbed in lust. The other girl shouted to her to close the door and she made a sad face as if to say, ‘Sorry for the late show but it's over now’ and she closed the door. I took a deep breath and went outside my apartment. I hoped that somehow one of them would see me through their window and feel the urge to have a conversation with me. The only thing interested in me were the mosquitoes so I quickly went back inside. I turned on my lights. Suddenly I noticed that practically every apartment that faced the girls had had their lights off and were turning them on as well. Obviously I wasn't the only one in my apartment building aware of their nightly exhibitions. On day four I took my place by the window with the lights off around 6:30pm. It was the last Friday of the month. Before I could make myself comfortable I saw the door swing wide open. Instead of my two naked nymphs I saw a tall, stern looking middle aged man carrying out a pair of suitcases. While he went out the apartment two young men who were probably his sons came and retrieved several of the the girls’ heavier belongings. As the young men left, my nymphs came out the door each holding light items. They were moving out. Based on the friendly banter among all of them it was clear that their evening exhibitionism was not a factor in their moving out. I felt heartbroken. I wanted to believe that their evening shows were for me and me only and it was only a matter of time before some form of communication took place between us. Instead they gave a good three day show and now they were gone. I wanted to find some kind of reason or excuse to go up to them and talk. ‘Do you guys need some help?’ Then I imagined their tall, stern faced father/uncle glaring at me with a murderous look and shaking his head. ‘We’re good. Thanks.’ I turned on the lights and peered at them boldly from my window. I wanted them to at least see me. The younger one was passing out the apartment and spotted me. She gave me a long curious stare while she walked and came across her sister/cousin and she began whispering in her ear and they both stopped and looked at me and then giggled. Feeling like a creep I drew back the curtains and came out of view. What now? Maybe they would stop by and say their goodbyes? Maybe I was just being pathetic? I lay in bed trying to ignore my conflicting feelings. In the shared kitchen I suddenly heard voices. Some of the boys in my apartment were hanging out or ‘liming’ as we call it here in Trinidad. They were talking about the girls who left and apparently one of them finally confided about seeing them naked at nights and they all started sharing stories of the girls’ daily naked ritual. Funny how they all never said a word to one another prior to this shared witnessing. They started some scuttlebutt on the identity of the girls and stories they heard about them from friends. Most of what they spoke of sounded like bullshit. I wanted to join in the conversation but it just seemed miserable. One of them was drunk and with a really high-pitched and whining voice and another spoke in such depravity that it was clear that given the chance he might’ve raped both girls. Outside I could hear a scuttling noise. The rat was making his rounds looking for fresh garbage. The rat was a much more industrious and respectable fellow than all of us humans who allowed the sight of two naked girls to turn us into primal beasts. I decided to call it a night.

Question: What movies with interesting concepts were poorly executed?
Answer: Looper (2012) ***Spoilers ahead*** Looper has the distinction of one of those rare movies. In the beginning it reminds me of why I love Hollywood and in the end it reminds me of why I hate Hollywood. Big budget Hollywood has mastered the art of dishing out movies that build imaginative concepts and develops intriguing characters and then by the halfway mark s**ts all over it with mindless action, tepid romance, explosions and low brow sci-fi for the sake of attracting all the Beavises and Buttheads out there. The story deals with bounty hunters who kill without discretion, victims sent from an agency in the future. The very same bounty hunters have an expiry date whereby when they reach a certain age they themselves are sent back to the past to be exterminated to 'close the loop.' Many times their own past selves are the ones who do such an extermination. Fascinating concept, and it gets even more fascinating when Bruce Willis' character escapes extermination from his younger self (Joseph Gordon Levitt) and then seeks to exterminate the guy who started this whole time travel assassination agency (The Rainmaker) while avoiding being killed by himself and several other 'loopers.’ Yeah rock on. Then somehow the movie takes us to a farm with some annoying kid and his mom, some soul searching and romance is flung into the mix, throw in a bunch of boring exposition, random telekinesis and super powers and the suddenly the movie turns into The Terminator meets Akira fanfiction. By the time the movie drew to a close (Joseph Gordon Levitt kills himself to eliminate his older self….big surprise) I yearn for the day time travel could be an actual possibility, so I could undo the precious time I wasted on this overrated movie.

Question: Why is Eric Clapton such a highly rated guitarist when he's very average?
Answer: Average you say? Clapton is in my personal top five of greatest guitarists. I'd even rank him higher than Hendrix and just a smidgen below Duane Allman. I dont know anything technical about guitars, I can't play and I definitely can't determine prowess. However I've listened to hundreds of guitar oriented albums and only a handful of guitarists stick out in terms of consistency of quality. Clapton is definitely one of them. For someone to listen to Disraeli Gears and call the stunning solos on that album average would be the rantings of a madman or the simply just a common troll. From his work with The Yardbirds, John Mayall & the Bluesbreakers, Cream, Blind Faith, Derek and the Dominos and his solo work (my least favourite, but heck he wrote Tears in Heaven) he has proven to be more than just average. I think the best performance depicting Clapton's talent is his guitar duel with The Band's Robbie Robertson for the The Last Waltz concert. Here one can see two immensely talented guitarists politely trying to upstage one another in a mastery of improvisation. The fans who wrote 'Clapton Is God’ on a London wall were not paid to do so. They did it because something about his guitar work touched them deeply inside that they felt him to be on a higher realm than ordinary people. Definitely doesn't fit the description of someone with average talent.

Question: At what age did you stop enjoying YA fiction?
Answer: I'm not hating on YA authors but I never saw the appeal. As a child Roald Dahl was my favorite author. I also read abridged and illustrated editions of the popular classics from Mark Twain, H.G. Wells, Arthur Conan Doyle, Dickens etc. As I entered my teens I attempted unabridged editions of the classics and voraciously read through my mother's bookshelf of adult novels. In my late teens I fell in love with The Good Earth by Pearl S. Buck and Angela's Ashes by Frank McCourt. I discovered early that I had a passion for historical stories of persistence through hardship, survival etc. YA books, to me, were for the kids who didn't really have a passion for reading and were off to a late start. YA books never had the charisma and imagination of children's books nor did they have the depth and seriousness of adult novels. They were just generic books written for overly self aware kids imho. I know I may sound pompous but I really didn't want to read about rich kids in school, girls dating the bad boy, broken friendships, parents divorcing or a boy and his dog surviving in some post apocalyptic future. I know there are good YA books out there but I really haven't come across one that appealed to me nor am I interested in looking for one at this stage in my life.
